parole.testo: Borrowed from Romani bokh (“hunger”); ultimately from Sanskrit बुभुक्षा (bubhukṣā). Reinforced and perhaps semantically influenced by Bock (etymology 1) in its sexual sense. First attested in the second half of the 20th century and originally belonging to the Rotwelsch cant. Distant doublet of Funkt
Borrowed from Romani ćhavo (“boy”). Cognates include Spanish chaval, possibly English chav.
Borrowed from Romani ćhaj (“girl”). Cf. Swedish tjej, Norwegian kjei, borrowed from the same source.

parole.significato: backwater, Hicksville, bumfuck (a backwards, boring rural town or village)
parole.testo: 19th century, from Romani gav (“village”), from Sanskrit ग्राम (grāma, “village”). Probably influenced by Rotwelsch kefar, from Hebrew כְּפָר (kfar, “village”); perhaps also by etymology 2 in the sense of “something worthless”. The now common plural in -er probably after Dörfer.
From Romani katšima, eventually from Proto-Slavic *kъrčьma. Doublet of regional Kretscham.

Unclear. Several possibilities have been suggested, including derivation from Romani [Term?] and derivation from Hebrew קוֹל (qōl, “voice”). But compare western German Kappes (“cabbage, nonsense”), though the second meaning might also be a loan translation of Kohl.

parole.significato: Rom (member of the Roma people), Romani
parole.testo: From Romani rrom (“Romani man”); see there for more.
Borrowed from Romani sáster (“iron”), from Sanskrit अस्त्र (astra, “missile weapon”).
